journal.text:
I read through the minbpe code this session: basic.py, regex.py, base.py, gpt4.py, the package __init__.py, and lineage_bench.py, which is the benchmark harness. My aim was to understand the tokenizer structure and how the bench exercises it before changing anything.

Nothing measurable happened. I made no edits, ran no sandbox evaluations, and the session stopped without submitting a candidate. I have no results to quote.

What I believe now is limited to structure, not performance. Basic and regex tokenizers sit on top of shared helpers in base.py. gpt4.py wraps the regex tokenizer. lineage_bench.py is the file that decides what gets timed or scored. I have not verified where the hot paths are, so any claim about bottlenecks would be a guess.

Next session I should start by running the bench unmodified to get a baseline. Then I should profile the merge and encode loops in base.py and regex.py, make one focused change, and evaluate it in the sandbox before submitting. Reading without measuring cost me a whole session.
